$comment: W29 G3b — the ONLY numbers this child chose for the outer shadow, written by
hand in one place. `build-shadow.py` merges them into the two committed 27
active documents and `seal.ts` re-resolves the digests; nothing else moves.
The objective is the shadow axis's `meanDeparture` — the mean of
(backdrop - rendered) over the whole exterior of the declared region, in
linear light — and not `falloffAmplitude`. That is a choice and it is the
one the instrument supports. `meanDeparture` is an exact integral over a
fixed population, defined on every cell including the ones whose normalised
block is absent; `falloffAmplitude` is one parameter of a two-parameter fit
to ring means, and where the 27 shadow's sigma falls to 1.5 device px there
are two or three rings above the body's own edge to fit it on. The amplitude
and sigma are reported beside every reading and the residual in them is
recorded (section 'sigmaIsNotSpanInvariantOn27' below); they are not what
was minimised.
The solve is the one `fit.py`'s header describes: render a candidate, read
the residual the law is stated in, move the candidate by that residual,
render again. Three rounds on the light bed (labels shadow-base, shadow-B,
shadow-C, with shadow-A discarded and shadow-D the lift's own round), two on
the dark bed and one on reduced transparency. Because the departure is very
nearly linear in the composited alpha at a fixed geometry, one round at a
known amplitude gives the geometry factor per cell and the required alpha
follows in closed form; the rounds after it are checks, not searches.

objective.metric: shadow.meanDeparture{Native,Web}, linear light, over the whole exterior of the declared region
objective.beforeUnits: mean |Web - Native| over 20 light standard cells at both scales

$comment: THE STRUCTURE THIS CHILD MEASURED AND COULD NOT FIT, named here and in
claims §5.154 rather than absorbed into a compromise that hides it.
On 26.5 the shadow's three lengths are span-invariant and that is a
positive measurement, not an absence: across spans 32, 44, 96 and 160 the
fitted sigma stays within 15.4-15.9 CSS px (MaterialOuterShadow's own
header). On 27 it does not. The native falloff sigma, in CSS px, reads
on the light standard bed, and the dark bed reads the same law (1.52 / 8.87
/ 13.42 / 17.43) as does reduced transparency (1.51 / 8.50 / 16.97). It is
linear in the casting span to within the reading's own noise:
sigma_css ~ 0.131 * (span - 26).
`MaterialOuterShadow.sigmaPx` is ONE constant and the shader reads it from a
uniform, so no value of it can be 1.8 at span 44 and 17.4 at span 160.
11.0 is the best single value the thick regime admits, because every row
this refit exists to clear (claims §5.153 §5) sits at span 96-160 where the
native reads 8.8-17.6. The thin cells keep a shadow that is about six times
too wide and, at the amplitude fitted beside it, carries the right ENERGY
in the wrong shape.
What would close it, and why this child did not build it: the casting
surface's span is already in the shader as `shadowAux.z` and
`outer_shadow_thick` already grades the AMPLITUDE by it, so the operator is
a span grading on the length rather than an architecture change. It is not
built here because Decision Log 6 (a) ruled the shadow's CONSTANTS refit and
contract X3 admits a new operator only where a named structure needs one —
and the constants alone take the departure residual from 0.0068 to 0.0007,
which is the ruling executed. Naming it is what this entry does instead, and
it is put to the user as Decision Log 7.

outerShadow.status: measured and fitted (W29 G3b, Decision Log 6 (a))
method: Apple's outer shadow moved on macOS 27 and G2 did not read it (claims §5.151
§2 lists the laws it read), so G3 was forbidden by X3 from following it and
recorded the finding instead (§5.153 §5). Decision Log 6 (a) ruled the read
and the refit. The read is native-against-native on the 27 bed at G2's own
bar, declared before the first 26.5 pair was opened
(`results/2026-09-19-w29-g3b-shadow-recede/bar-declaration.md`): the shadow
moved on EVERY measurable cell of every profile — 342 of 342 on the mean
departure, 246 of 246 on the fitted sigma and amplitude — at a median
delta/bar of 10^5 to 10^7.
sigmaPx 15.55 -> 11.0. The native sigma is no longer span-invariant (see
`sigmaIsNotSpanInvariantOn27` in fitted-shadow.json); 11.0 is the best single
value for the thick regime, where every row this refit exists to clear sits.
The amplitudes are solved from the departure. At sigma 11 with the 26.5
amplitudes the web reads 0.00648 / 0.01350 / 0.03052 on the checkerboard
capsule / rrect-md / rrect-ml against a 27 native of 0.00082 / 0.00379 /
0.01270, so the composited alpha each regime needs is the 26.5 alpha times
that ratio, and the occlusion follows by inverting sRGB's 2.4 power. Over the
three supported backdrops the thin regime wants 0.041-0.056, the 96 anchor
0.101-0.119 and the 128 anchor 0.192-0.209; the adopted numbers are those
means.
thickOcclusionAt160 is UNFITTED, as its 26.5 value was and for the same
reason: every span above 128 in the bed is holdout. 0.293 is the linear
extrapolation from the two fitted anchors, and the native corroborates the
shape rather than the value — its own falloff amplitude rises 0.1074 ->
0.1819 -> 0.2586 across spans 96 / 128 / 160, increments of 0.0745 and
0.0767, which is a straight line to 3 %.
liftAmplitude 0.01 -> 0.001, fitted on its own round. At 0 the bed-wide
signed departure residual is +0.00068 and at 0.004 it is -0.00186, so the
zero crossing is at 0.0011 and the lift is about a tenth of its 26.5 value.
The 27 shadow still adds light — it is not stood down — but far less of it.
reducedTransparencyOcclusion 0.197 -> 0.087, solved the same way on the
reduced-transparency profile's four identified active cells (checkerboard and
photo, capsule and rrect-md). **It is a compromise where 26.5's was a
measurement**: the 26.5 reference's exterior under the preference was flat at
0.192-0.202 thin and thick together, which is what justifies the fold writing
one amplitude into all six anchors. On 27 it is not flat — the native falloff
amplitude reads 0.165 at span 44, 0.111 at 96 and 0.251 at 160 — so the four
cells want 0.024 to 0.053 of alpha and 0.087 is their mean. Recorded as a
residual of the fold, not of the fit.
offsetPx, spreadPx, thinOcclusionDark, sizeGain, liftSpanMin, liftSpanFull
and liftBlurSigmaCss do NOT move, each for a reason. The offset is span-graded
on 27 like the sigma (4.0 CSS px at span 44, 7.5 at 96, 8.0 at 128) and 7.95
is already right where the rows are. thinOcclusionDark stays 0 because the
shadow is still analytically inert over black: the native reads 0.00000 over
`dark-solid` at span 44 and 0.00006 at span 96.

outerShadow.status: measured and fitted (W29 G3b, Decision Log 6 (a))
method: The dark bed reads the SAME geometry law as the light one — native falloff
sigma 1.52 / 8.87 / 13.42 / 17.43 CSS px at spans 44 / 96 / 128 / 160 against
the light bed's 1.84 / 8.80 / 13.10 / 17.30 — so sigmaPx takes the same 11.0.
It is a NEW key in this patch: the 26.5 dark document names no length at all
and inherited the default's 15.55, and a document that now differs from the
default there has to say so.
The amplitude is where the two schemes part. On the light bed the shadow's
amplitude roughly halved between the beds; on the dark bed the native's own
falloff amplitude did NOT move (median 27/26.5 ratio 1.02) and the whole fall
in its departure is the sigma. So the dark thin regime goes 0.063 -> 0.032 and
the 96 anchor 0.278 -> 0.126, both solved from the departure at sigma 11 on
the four identified dark calibration cells (checkerboard and photo, capsule
and rrect-md, at both scales).
thickOcclusionAt128 and thickOcclusionAt160 are UNFITTED and derived, because
the dark bed declares no calibration cell above span 96 — the same position
its 26.5 values were in. They carry the LIGHT document's fitted span shape
scaled to this document's 96 anchor (0.202/0.111 and 0.293/0.111), and the
native corroborates the shape: the dark native's amplitude ratio between
spans 160 and 96 is 2.46 and 2.55 on its two supported backdrops against the
light bed's 2.41.
liftAmplitude 0.0051 -> 0.0005, carried at the light document's fitted ratio
(0.001/0.01) because the lift shows over a BRIGHT backdrop and the dark bed
declares none outside holdout and probe. Derived, not fitted, and named here
as such.
reducedTransparencyOcclusion stays at its 26.5 value of 0.038. There is no
dark reduced-transparency profile on either bed, so the constant is
identified by nothing on 27 exactly as it was on 26.5, and moving it on a
scaled derivation would put an invented number where an unidentified one is
already honestly recorded.
